items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I was taking orchestral repertoire with Bill Vacchiano... We both start playing. We both start playing the thing... and we look at each other. We start laughing.

ctx.x: So, what was that experience like at the Manhattan School? Did you study classical trumpet? Or did you study . . . ?

Oh yes. I studied – I was taking orchestral repertoire with Bill Vacchiano, who was at that time first trumpet player with the Philharmonic. I also studied with Joseph Alessi, Sr., Mr. Alessi, who was probably – he was like a father. He was one of – his grandson is the first trombone player with the New York Philharmonic. He – his grandfather died when he was an infant. So he never saw his grandfather, never knew his grandfather. But this was one of the most wonderful men that ever lived. He was just great. I…
Did you ever consider it? Did you ever think, “Boy, I did really want to play in a symphony. Maybe I could move to Dallas”? Or was it just . . . ?
